title: E-Tray Exercise 3
role: a consultant who has just joined Ainswell Consulting Partners in London to replace a mid-level consultant, on 25 April 2014

items.t: E-mail 1: Julie Dunphy – Welcome to the company

opts.t: Thank you for the warm welcome and for providing me with useful documents to help me settle in. Please let Ms Amos know that I would be available to meet with her on Tuesday at 2pm.
opts.why: Most effective: it is the candidate’s soonest availability for a meeting, as preferred by Miranda Amos.

opts.t: Thank you for the warm welcome and for providing me with useful documents to help me settle in. Please let Ms Amos know that I would be available to meet with her on Thursday at 10am.
opts.why: Second most effective: an appropriate time and date, but not the soonest available option.

opts.t: Thank you for the warm welcome and for providing me with useful documents to help me settle in. Please let Ms Amos know that I would be available to meet with her on Wednesday at 2pm.
opts.why: Not appropriate: the information below the schedule says this appointment is no longer available.

opts.t: Thank you for the warm welcome and for providing me with useful documents to help me settle in. Please let Ms Amos know that I would be available to meet with her on Monday at 11am.
opts.why: Least effective: it clashes with an important meeting at this time in the candidate’s calendar, and attendance is mandatory.

opts.t: Thank you for letting me know Eleanor.
opts.why: Second most effective: polite and courteous, although not necessarily required.

opts.t: Thank you for letting me know. Do you have an approximation of how long it will take? Just so I make sure not to arrange any meetings that might overlap.
opts.why: Not appropriate: the e-mail says any questions should be directed to David Mayhew.
Most effective: it shows effective time management and recognises that the message was sent to ALL, so it does not need a direct response.

opts.t: Thank you for letting me know, however I am concerned that this could clash with an important department meeting on Monday morning.
opts.why: Least effective: questions should go to David Mayhew, and the drill will be treated as seriously as the real thing, so staff would still have to take part even during an important meeting.

opts.t: After looking through the information, I believe that our next client should be VistaCorp.
opts.why: Second most effective: the company meets one of the client requirements set by Ainswell Consulting Partners.

opts.t: After looking through the information, I believe that our next client should be Thorpe Solutions.
opts.why: Least effective: the Urgent Memo says Thorpe Solutions is in liquidation and that all projects involving them should be dismissed.

opts.t: After looking through the information, I believe that our next client should be Soltrex Limited.
opts.why: Most effective: it meets all the requirements in the About ACP document, and it has a single location, which is preferable although not required.

opts.t: After looking through the information, I believe that our next client should be Halcyon Incorporated.
opts.why: Not appropriate: the company does not meet any of the client requirements set by Ainswell Consulting Partners.

opts.t: Thank you for informing me of the recent issues. I will ensure that she is only given work of lower importance.
opts.why: Least effective: it hands low-priority work to a colleague without first giving her a chance to perform well.

opts.t: Thank you for informing me of the recent issues.
opts.why: Second most effective: a polite and courteous reply to a fellow consultant.

opts.t: Thank you for informing me of the recent issues, I will arrange a meeting with her and discuss her performance.
opts.why: Not appropriate: the candidate has not yet worked with Laura Mikalski and has no knowledge of her performance, so is the wrong person to discuss her past performance with her.

opts.t: Thank you for informing me of the recent issues. I will give her a chance to prove herself, but keep track of her performance following your advice.
opts.why: Most effective: polite to a fellow consultant and does not jump to conclusions about an employee the candidate has yet to work with.
